event_questions.label: E1
event_questions.not_this: A defect the claim itself attributes wholly to the tenant, or says he must remedy at his own expense, is no. A cause the claim calls shared or disputed is open, not no; a landlord's allegation that the tenant caused it, which the claim disputes, does not make this no.
event_questions.question: Does the claim state that the rented dwelling has a defect (for example mould, damp, or heating that fails) or that the tenant is disturbed in using the dwelling as agreed, without the claim itself saying that the tenant alone caused the defect or must remedy it at his own expense?

event_questions.label: E2
event_questions.not_this: No: only a file stating that no notice of termination has been given at all (also a lease of limited duration that simply ends on its agreed date, a termination only announced or threatened, a notice given by the tenant). A notice the landlord says was sent and the tenant says never reached him is open, not no.
event_questions.question: Has the landlord given the tenant notice terminating the lease of the dwelling, and has it reached the tenant?

questions.label: Q1
questions.not_this: An increase the landlord justifies by general inflation or by cost increases without an index clause in the lease.
questions.question: Does the claim state that the increase applies a clause of the lease linking the rent to an index (such as the Swiss consumer price index)?

questions.label: Q2
questions.not_this: A landlord's plan to raise the rent that has not been announced, demanded or charged; the initial rent agreed for a new lease; new accessory charges or reduced services without a higher rent.
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord has announced, demanded or charged a higher rent for the dwelling, by a notice, a letter, an invoice or otherwise (whether or not on an official form)?

questions.label: Q3
questions.not_this: An increase under an index clause; an increase the lease does not fix in advance.
questions.question: Does the claim state that the increase is a step fixed in advance in the lease, by which the rent rises periodically by fixed amounts (graduated rent)?

questions.label: Q4
questions.not_this: An increase justified only by rents customary in the locality (art. 269a let. a) or by inflation on the risk capital (art. 269a let. e).
questions.question: Does the increase notice give, as its reason, higher costs for the landlord (for example higher mortgage interest or operating costs) or additional services or works by the landlord (for example a renovation)?

questions.label: Q5
questions.not_this: A threat of termination without a notice of termination (it shows on the increase notice or its covering letter, which is requested anyway); a notice of termination given separately at another time.
questions.question: Does the claim state that, together with the rent increase, the landlord gave notice of termination?

routing.question: Which tenancy dispute does the claim concern: a defect of the dwelling or a disturbance of its agreed use that the tenant did not cause (for example mould, damp, or heating that fails), a termination of the lease by the landlord, or a rent increase? A rent increase that the landlord accompanied with a notice of termination is a rent increase dispute: the rent-increase rules examine that notice (art. 269d para. 2 let. c).

text:
Good morning,

On 5 May 2026 all the tenants at Dorfstrasse 55 in Thun got a short letter saying the building has been sold and that Feldegg Trading Ltd, represented by Mr Paul Fankhauser, is now our landlord. Since then there has been a lot of nervous talk in the stairwell.

Let me be clear about where things stand for me: Feldegg has not asked me for a higher rent. There has been no letter, no form and no new bill with a different amount. The May and June payments went out at the same CHF 1340 I've been paying since I moved in in spring 2022, and Mr Fankhauser hasn't said anything about the rent going up, not even informally.

I also checked my lease from the previous owner. There is no clause tying the rent to the consumer price index or any other index. The rent is just a fixed figure.

My neighbour Rachel Zimmermann is convinced that new owners always try to squeeze more out of existing tenants, and she has me worried. What I'd like to understand is this: does my existing lease simply carry on unchanged with the new owner? And if Feldegg did want to raise my rent at some point, what would they have to do, and what could I do in response? I'd rather know now than be caught off guard.

Thank you for your time,
Alice Reid
